inputs.share_count_basis: 294.68m equity shares on issue at 31 March 2026 (weighted average 294.679m per FY2026 AR EPS note), INCLUDING the treasury shares held by the ESOP trust. Diluted weighted average for EPS is 294.31m; the full issued count is used as the conservative fully diluted figure. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and there is no pending non-SBC issuance (the Kesoram share issue completed in FY2025).
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company-defined consolidated net debt at 30 September 2026 (Q2 FY2027 presentation, Financial position slide): gross debt Rs 28,411 cr less treasury surplus Rs 4,875 cr = Rs 23,536 cr. Gross debt is borrowings only (ties to balance-sheet borrowings; lease liabilities of Rs 974 cr at March 2026 are excluded, see lease_treatment). Treasury surplus is cash plus liquid investments.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted: UltraTech is a net-debt company, and under its Ind AS presentation interest and dividend income (Rs 2,614m in FY2026) is already removed from operating cash flow and shown in investing, as is interest paid (financing). Reported OCF is therefore already an unlevered, ex-treasury-income figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Compensation Expenses under Employees Stock Options Scheme' Rs 51.96 cr (CSV StockBasedComp 519.6). Equity-award taxes nil (options are settled through an ESOP trust that buys treasury shares).
inputs.buyback_note: Not a buyback programme: Rs 119.35 cr of treasury shares purchased by the ESOP trust in FY2026 (Rs 50.01 cr received back on option exercise). The trust purchases are what keeps the count flat, so the flat-count convention is funded.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:10Z (15:28 IST Friday, the final minutes of the NSE regular session; effectively the regular close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows. India 10-year G-sec ~6.6% + beta ~0.9 (large-cap cement, less cyclical than steel) x India equity risk premium ~6.5% = cost of equity ~12.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~7.6%, ~5.7% after tax. Market-value weights: net debt Rs 235bn against ~Rs 3.57tn market cap = ~6% debt. WACC = 0.94 x 12.5% + 0.06 x 5.7% = ~12.1%, set at 12.0%, in line with the other INR builds in this folder (TATASTEEL.NS 12.0, LT.NS 12.0). Same WACC in all three scenarios: overcapacity, input-cost and integration risk are carried in the flows and the weights, not the rate. No leverage premium: net debt/EBITDA is ~1.2x after the special dividend, investment grade, and the H1 FY2027 rise in net debt was a one-off distribution, not operating stress. Terminal growth 5.0% INR nominal (~4% RBI inflation target + ~1% real); at 12%/5% Gordon equals 15x, which is also the cap chosen for a cyclical commodity producer, so the two bind together in the base case.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Consolidated lease payments including interest were Rs 276.29 cr in FY2026 (0.31% of revenue: Rs 216.53 cr principal + Rs 59.76 cr interest, both in financing) and are charged every year through lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (Rs 974 cr) are excluded from net debt. D&A paths are ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2026: 46,444.6 total less 2,019.6 ROU = 44,425, 5.02% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in taxable EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are fully consolidated (100% of India Cements and the overseas subsidiaries); the non-controlling interest is deducted once in the equity bridge at its 31 March 2026 book value of Rs 4,088.90 cr. NCI rose from Rs 3,186.59 cr because UltraTech sold its India Cements holding down from 81.49% to 74.99% to meet the minimum public shareholding rule.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations. UltraTech is an operating manufacturer (India's largest cement producer, 210.1 mtpa), not a financial or property vehicle, so the routing table's 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' row applies. FRESH BUILD, no prior DCF. EBITDA BASIS: margins are OPERATING EBITDA (CSV EBITDA less other income; FY2026 = 175,977 - 5,775 = 170,202, 19.2% of revenue). Other income is excluded from the flows and its source assets are in the bridge: treasury surplus inside net debt, non-current investments as a bridge item. H1 FY2027 NET DEBT: the rise from Rs 16,620 cr (March 2026) to Rs 23,536 cr (September 2026) is almost entirely the Rs 240/share FY2026 dividend (Rs 7,072 cr, approved at the 17 August 2026 AGM, against Rs 77.50 the year before). H1 FY2027 free cash flow to equity was positive at Rs 388 cr. It was not debt-funded M&A; the India Cements and Kesoram acquisitions closed in FY2025. That dividend has left the company and is NOT available to a buyer at today's price, so the September net debt is the correct anchor. TIMING: flows start with full-year FY2027 while net debt is at the half-year; the overlap is H1 FY2027 FCFE of Rs 388 cr, about Rs 13 per share, ignored. DEBT HISTORY: FY2016-FY2020 total debt in the CSV is understated (current maturities sit in other liabilities); nothing in this model uses those years' debt. FY2025 includes part-year India Cements and Kesoram, so FY2025-FY2026 growth overstates organic growth. SBC is 0.06% of revenue, so house and street bases are nearly identical and band_position carries no information. last_fcf follows the house identity (reported FCF less SBC); on the lease-adjusted basis the model uses, FY2026 owner FCF is Rs 2,763m lower at ~53,100.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest at book (mainly 25% of India Cements)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR consolidated balance sheet, 31 March 2026; flows are 100% consolidated
Q2 FY2027 presentation, consolidated financial position at 30 September 2026 (Rs 1,779 cr); their income is excluded from operating EBITDA

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (11.6%) is 32% above the EPS 5-year CAGR (7.9%) and 26% below the revenue 5-year CAGR (14.6%). Equity and revenue were lifted by acquisitions (Kesoram paid in shares, India Cements consolidated) while EPS started from the FY2021 margin peak (operating EBITDA margin 25.9% against 19.2% in FY2026). Per-share earning power has grown more slowly than the asset base.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; no interest-income adjustment is needed because OCF already excludes it). FY2021 owner FCF of 105,660 was a capex trough (4.3% of revenue) at a margin peak; FY2023 was 28,328 and FY2026 55,861. The series is dominated by the capex cycle (4% of revenue in FY2021, 11-13% in FY2024-FY2026), so neither FCF CAGR is a usable growth anchor. Operating EBITDA margin history: FY2016 19.1, FY2017 20.5, FY2018 19.6, FY2019 18.2, FY2020 22.0, FY2021 25.9, FY2022 21.9, FY2023 16.8, FY2024 18.3, FY2025 16.5, FY2026 19.2; ten-year average 19.8%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027: Q2 revenue +18.9% on volume +12.9%, H1 EBITDA +14%; second-half comparisons are tougher. FY2028-FY2029: capacity goes from 210 mtpa to above 240 mtpa by FY2028 against industry demand growth of 7-8%, plus a first contribution from wires and cables. Then volume growth of 5-6% plus 1-2% price, fading to 6% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Operating EBITDA margin. FY2027 at 19.0% (H1 running about level with FY2026's 19.2% despite fuel and packaging inflation). Matures at 20.5%, slightly above the ten-year average of 19.8%, for the waste-heat and green-power cost programme and acquired-plant integration, but well short of the Rs 1,400/t aspiration because the whole industry is adding capacity.
base.capex_rationale: Rs 16,000-17,000 cr committed through FY2028 plus Rs 1,800 cr for wires and cables puts FY2027 at about Rs 10,500 cr. A market leader holding share in a market growing 6-8% has to keep adding roughly 12-15 mtpa a year, so capex stays 8-9% of revenue through the middle years and settles at 6.5% (1.3x depreciation) for 5% terminal growth.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax on EBIT. FY2026 cash tax was only ~10.5% of operating EBIT (refunds and accelerated depreciation); H1 FY2027 taxes paid of Rs 981 cr annualise to ~16%. Ramps to the 25.2% statutory rate as the deferred-tax shield from the capex programme unwinds.
base.wc_rationale: Net working capital is slightly negative (-Rs 1,400 cr) and has swung both ways (FY2025 outflow, FY2026 inflow, H1 FY2027 outflow). Held neutral.

scenario_narratives.base: Volume keeps outgrowing the industry as capacity moves from 210 mtpa to above 240 mtpa by FY2028 and the Kesoram and India Cements plants are run under the UltraTech brand, but the same wave of industry additions (Adani's Ambuja/ACC and others, ~150 mtpa sector-wide through FY2028) keeps realisations roughly flat in real terms. Operating EBITDA per tonne creeps from ~Rs 1,100 to ~Rs 1,200 on waste-heat recovery and green power rather than on price, so the margin matures at 20.5%, a little above its ten-year average. Capex stays heavy because holding a 28-30% share of a growing market means building 12-15 mtpa every year. Wires and cables becomes a modest, capital-consuming adjacency. Revenue reaches ~Rs 1.95tn in FY2036 with an owner-FCF margin near 10%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Industry consolidation produces pricing discipline: the two large groups control over half of capacity, utilisation climbs through the high 70s as government infrastructure and housing demand absorbs the new plants, and UltraTech gets most of the way to its Rs 1,400/t aspiration (23% margin, last seen only in the FY2020-FY2022 upcycle). Green power reaches the 85% target and structurally lowers power and fuel cost, acquired assets reach network utilisation, and Ultravolt scales through the existing dealer network to a mid-single-digit share of revenue. Growth stays in double digits through FY2031.
scenario_narratives.bear: Overcapacity bites. Sector additions outrun demand in FY2028-FY2029, a state-election and monsoon-disrupted demand year coincides with imported pet-coke and crude-linked packaging inflation, and realisations fall as Adani prices for share. Operating EBITDA margin drops back to the FY2023/FY2025 trough of 16.5% and recovers only to 17.5%. The committed capex is spent anyway, so FY2027-FY2028 free cash flow is thin and net debt/EBITDA drifts toward 2x before capex is cut back to near-maintenance. Wires and cables earns below its cost of capital against Polycab and KEI. This is a margin-compression case, not a solvency case; the terminal value does not hit the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default, because sector-wide overcapacity is the single high-severity risk in the analysis and it is already visible (71% utilisation in Q2 FY2027, margins three points below the last upcycle); it is a profitability risk only, since leverage is ~1.2x EBITDA. Base 50%: the path follows the committed capacity roadmap and the ten-year average margin. Bull 25%, below the 35% default, because it needs three independent things at once: industry pricing discipline during a capacity wave, benign fuel costs, and a successful entry into an unrelated business.

valuation_philosophy.summary: UltraTech is the scale and cost leader in a growing market, but cement is a capital-heavy commodity: return on capital employed has run 10-14% for a decade (12% in FY2026), close to an INR cost of capital of 12%, and growth has to be bought with capex of 8-11% of revenue. A business that earns roughly its cost of capital on new investment is worth a modest premium to its invested capital, which is what this model returns (about 1.8x September 2026 book value of ~Rs 2,500 per share in the base case). The market price is about 4.7x book and roughly 20x EV to FY2027 EBITDA, a multiple that requires either a much lower discount rate than 12% or returns on incremental capital well above anything in the ten-year record. The gap between value and price is therefore a statement about Indian large-cap multiples and the discount rate, not about the quality of the company, and it is consistent with the other INR builds in this folder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: at 12% WACC and 5% growth Gordon equals the 15x cap. A reader who accepts 10% for a dominant Indian franchise gets a materially higher value, but the 15x cap still binds, so the sensitivity grid understates how much of the market price is explained by a lower required return.
Mature margin: each point of operating EBITDA margin is worth roughly Rs 350-400 per share in the base case; the Rs 1,400/t aspiration (bull) against the 16.5% trough (bear) is the main axis.

Capex intensity: the terminal 6.5% of revenue assumes growth capacity keeps costing what it does today; cheaper brownfield or acquired capacity would lift free cash flow, another greenfield race would cut it.
Upside the model does not carry: further distressed acquisitions below replacement cost, and wires and cables earning above its cost of capital.
Downside the model does not carry: a second large special dividend or debt-funded acquisition lifting leverage, and legacy legal liabilities at India Cements and Kesoram.
